reading: The grid is cut into cells by separator lines; exactly four separator crossings are background-coloured. Output is the sub-grid whose corners are those four crossings (inclusive).

new_rows.name: gap
new_rows.datalog: gap(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), A = X - 1, B = X + 1, U = Y - 1, D = Y + 1, cell(Y, A, K), cell(Y, B, K), cell(U, X, K), cell(D, X, K).

why: exactly four background cells have all four orthogonal neighbours of one same non-background colour; the output equals the input box spanned by them
invariants: cell contents inside the box are copied unchanged

reading: The single 8 shape moves down one row and is recoloured to 2.
why: output shape is the input shape translated by (+1,0) with colour 8 replaced by 2

reading: Each 5x5 window with an all-0 border has a 3x3 interior; every 0 cell of that interior is replaced by a fixed positional digit (176/405/293, centre stays 0); 8 cells stay.

slots.anchor: each 5x5 box whose border ring is all colour 0
slots.mask: only interior cells that are 0 are painted; 8 cells unchanged

why: every changed cell is a 0 inside a window interior and becomes template[row][col] of its interior position

reading: Each row has one 5; the whole output row is painted by the column of that 5: column 0 -> 2, column 1 -> 4, column 2 -> 3.

slots.key: column index -> colour {0:2, 1:4, 2:3}, learned from train

why: each output row is uniform and its colour depends only on the column of the 5 in that input row

reading: Nine 3x3 pieces (mostly 5 with coloured corner/edge cells) are scattered on a 0 background; they are assembled into a 9x9 square, each piece placed in the 3x3 slot matching where its coloured cells sit (corner pieces to corners, edge pieces to edges, plain 5 block in the centre).

slots.slot: position in a 3x3 layout determined by which side/corner of the piece carries non-5 colour

why: output is a 3x3 arrangement of exactly the input pieces, unrotated, with coloured parts facing outward

reading: Solid rectangles of 0 at least 2x2 are filled with 2; where candidate rectangles overlap, only those not overlapped by a strictly larger one are filled.

new_rows.name: zrect
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
vr(Y, Y, X) :- z(Y, X).
vr(A, B2, X) :- vr(A, B, X), B2 = B + 1, z(B2, X).
rc(A, B, X, X) :- vr(A, B, X).
rc(A, B, P, Q2) :- rc(A, B, P, Q), Q2 = Q + 1, vr(A, B, Q2).
big(A, B, P, Q) :- rc(A, B, P, Q), B > A, Q > P.
area(A, B, P, Q, count(Y, X)) :- big(A, B, P, Q), z(Y, X), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q.
beaten(A, B, P, Q) :- area(A, B, P, Q, N), area(A2, B2, P2, Q2, M), M > N, A2 <= B, A <= B2, P2 <= Q, P <= Q2.
zrect(Y, X) :- area(A, B, P, Q, N), !beaten(A, B, P, Q), z(Y, X), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q.

why: every 0 cell in a kept all-0 rectangle (both sides >= 2, no overlapping strictly larger such rectangle) becomes 2; nothing else changes
invariants: 0 cells not in a kept rectangle

reading: The single 2 cell is erased and its four diagonal neighbours get fixed colours: up-left 3, up-right 6, down-left 8, down-right 7 (clipped at the border).
why: output is the 3x3 unit 3.6/.../8.7 centred on the marker, clipped to the grid, everything else 0

reading: Inside the 0 region, the longest diagonal run of 0 that starts in a corner pocket (cell whose upper and side neighbours toward the run's back are walls) is recoloured 8.
why: the changed cells are exactly one maximal diagonal 0-run starting at a corner pocket, the unique longest such run, and 0 -> 8 on it

reading: Pairs of 2x2 blocks of 8 sit on the same two rows; the cells strictly between each pair are cut out and the cut strips are stacked top to bottom.

slots.brackets: pairs of 2x2 colour-8 squares sharing the same two rows
slots.piece: the 2-row strip strictly between the two squares of a pair
slots.output: pieces stacked vertically in top-to-bottom order (all same width)

why: each 2-row band of the output equals the input cells between one bracket pair

reading: Count the 8-connected objects of each non-background colour; draw a bottom-aligned bar chart of width 5 where each colour has a fixed column (5,2,8,9,6 left to right) and bar height = its object count; height = max count, empty cells are 7.

slots.bar: count cells of that colour stacked from the bottom

why: each output column holds k cells of its colour at the bottom where k is the number of objects of that colour in the input
